nodes.label: Distributed Tracing
nodes.rationale: OpenTelemetry traces show where time and failures move across service boundaries, complementing metrics that reveal that a problem exists and logs that explain a specific event.

nodes.label: RED and USE Metrics
nodes.rationale: Request paths are measured by rate, errors, and duration; resources use utilization, saturation, and errors, with bounded labels and percentiles rather than averages.

nodes.label: Core Web Vitals Targets
nodes.rationale: LCP, INP, and CLS thresholds provide shared good, needs-improvement, and poor targets for frontend performance.

nodes.label: N+1 Query Elimination
nodes.rationale: Measured query waterfalls are corrected with joins, bounded retrieval, indexes, and caching rather than speculative micro-optimizations.

nodes.label: Metric Threshold Rollback
nodes.rationale: Error rate, latency, client errors, and business metrics have explicit advance, hold, and rollback thresholds for each rollout stage.

nodes.label: Development Lifecycle Sequence
nodes.rationale: A feature may progress from intent through specification, planning, implementation, telemetry, adversarial review, testing, review, documentation, migration, and launch, with only the relevant skills applied.

nodes.label: Skill Discovery and Routing
nodes.rationale: Tasks are routed to the workflow appropriate to their current development phase, with multiple skills applied when one task crosses concerns.

nodes.label: On-Call Instrumentation Questions
nodes.rationale: Telemetry is designed around the questions an on-call engineer must answer; signals without an operational question become noise.

nodes.label: Measure Identify Fix Verify
nodes.rationale: Performance work begins with synthetic and real-user baselines, targets the measured bottleneck, verifies the result, and guards against regression instead of optimizing assumptions.

nodes.label: Definition of Done
nodes.rationale: Completion requires evidence: tests pass, regressions are absent, runtime behavior is verified, and documentation is updated.

nodes.label: Strangler Pattern
nodes.rationale: Old and new systems run in parallel while traffic shifts incrementally, reducing cutover risk before the old implementation is removed.

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Records
nodes.rationale: ADRs capture consequential technical choices, their status, context, alternatives, and consequences using the repository's established documentation convention.

nodes.label: ADR Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: ADRs move from proposed to accepted and then to superseded or deprecated; old records remain to preserve historical context.

nodes.label: Contract-First Slicing
nodes.rationale: Backend and frontend work can proceed in parallel only after a shared API contract lets each side implement and test against the same boundary.

nodes.label: Risk-First Slicing
nodes.rationale: The riskiest or most uncertain technical path is proved first so failure occurs before substantial dependent work is built.

nodes.label: Thin Vertical Slices
nodes.rationale: Each increment implements the smallest complete user path, then tests, verifies, and commits it before expanding the system.

nodes.label: Vertical Task Slicing
nodes.rationale: Each task delivers a complete working feature path across required layers rather than postponing integration until a large horizontal phase ends.

nodes.label: Code Is a Liability
nodes.rationale: Every line carries maintenance, security, dependency, and onboarding cost, so functionality should be delivered with less code and complexity when practical.

nodes.label: Safe Incremental Migration
nodes.rationale: A replacement must exist and be proven before deprecation, consumers should migrate one at a time with verification, and removal should occur only after active usage reaches zero.

nodes.label: Decision Rationale
nodes.rationale: High-value documentation preserves context, constraints, alternatives, and trade-offs so future engineers understand why an expensive decision was made.

nodes.label: Structured Correlation Logging
nodes.rationale: Stable event names, machine-readable fields, correlation IDs, and explicit entry points reconstruct individual distributed runs while secrets and full PII remain excluded.

nodes.label: Parameterized Queries
nodes.rationale: Values are passed separately from SQL text so user input cannot alter query structure.

nodes.label: Secure Session Cookies
nodes.rationale: Session secrets come from the environment and cookies are httpOnly, secure, sameSite, and time-bounded.

nodes.label: SSRF Defense
nodes.rationale: User-influenced URLs are restricted by scheme and host, all DNS results must be public unicast addresses, redirects are forbidden, and high-risk flows must address DNS-rebinding gaps.

nodes.label: Supply Chain Hardening
nodes.rationale: Dependency installation boundaries, scripts, lockfile audits, reachability, provenance, and immutable installs are reviewed together because audits only detect known advisories.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Boundary System
nodes.rationale: Always-do controls are non-negotiable, ask-first changes require human approval, and never-do rules prohibit unsafe shortcuts such as committed secrets or client-only trust.

nodes.label: Detect Fetch Implement Cite
nodes.rationale: Detect exact stack versions, fetch the relevant documentation, implement documented version-specific patterns, and make each decision verifiable.

nodes.label: Official Documentation Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Official documentation, official blogs, web standards, and compatibility data are preferred over tutorials, community answers, AI summaries, and stale memory.

nodes.label: Threat Model First
nodes.rationale: Controls are designed only after trust boundaries, valuable assets, STRIDE threats, and abuse cases are explicit because security failures often originate in design.

nodes.label: Documentation Retrieval Safety
nodes.rationale: Fetched pages are untrusted data: model-directed instructions are ignored and only framework signal is extracted, with conflicts surfaced instead of silently resolved.

nodes.label: Abstract Diagonal Ribbon Mark
nodes.rationale: The visible mark consists of broad angular dark-gray bands separated by narrow negative-space channels, producing an abstract geometric symbol at very small scale; the exact intended letterform is uncertain.

nodes.label: Browser Site Identification
nodes.rationale: The favicon filename, public web-asset location, compact dimensions, and simplified mark strongly indicate use for browser-tab, bookmark, or shortcut recognition.

nodes.label: Monochrome Dark-Gray Design
nodes.rationale: All visible opaque pixels use closely related charcoal-gray values around #343434, with no distinct accent colors.

nodes.label: VibeCoder Brand Mark
nodes.rationale: The asset is the Vibecoder repository's favicon and is positioned to function as a compact product identity mark, although the image itself contains no explicit wordmark.

nodes.label: Compact Web Brand Icon
nodes.rationale: The tiny dimensions, simple flat-color silhouette, and transparent edges make the asset suitable for small browser or application placements; the PNG itself does not encode the exact consuming surface.

nodes.label: Coral-Red Monochrome Palette
nodes.rationale: The visible pixels use a single vivid coral-red hue centered around #fd3535; the slight RGB differences are edge anti-aliasing and alpha variation rather than separate colored elements.

nodes.label: Next.js App Icon Role
nodes.rationale: In the Next.js App Router, a PNG named icon under src/app is the conventional application icon asset, so this path identifies the intended app and browser icon role.

nodes.label: Three-Component Abstract Mark
nodes.rationale: The 19 by 19 image contains a vivid red abstract mark made from three broad, rounded components separated by clear negative spaces; it is a compact geometric logomark rather than text, a scene, or a data visualization.

nodes.label: Transparent Alpha Canvas
nodes.rationale: The PNG is 19 by 19 with an RGBA alpha channel and no opaque background rectangle, leaving the mark isolated for compositing on different interface backdrops.

nodes.label: VibeCoder Brand Identity
nodes.rationale: The icon.png filename, Next.js app-route location, and matching red three-component mark indicate VibeCoder's visual identity; the image contains no written wordmark.

nodes.label: VibeCoder Favicon PNG Asset
nodes.rationale: A 19 by 19 pixel PNG stored at the conventional favicon path and optimized with alpha transparency for compact browser-facing display.

nodes.label: Claim Extract Doubt Cycle
nodes.rationale: The workflow states a claim, extracts the smallest artifact and contract, invokes an adversarial reviewer, reconciles findings, and stops when the risk justifies ending the cycle.

nodes.label: Cross-Model Review Escalation
nodes.rationale: A different model architecture can expose blind spots shared by the author and a single-model reviewer, but the interactive user decides whether the extra cost is worthwhile.

nodes.label: Acceptance-Criteria Tasks
nodes.rationale: Tasks specify testable acceptance conditions, verification commands, dependencies, likely files, scope, and periodic checkpoints.

nodes.label: Dependency Graph
nodes.rationale: Implementation follows dependencies bottom-up so foundations and risky prerequisites exist before dependent work begins.

nodes.label: Prove-It Pattern
nodes.rationale: A bug fix begins with a regression test that fails for the reported reason, then passes after the fix, and is followed by the full suite.

nodes.label: Red Green Refactor
nodes.rationale: A failing test defines the behavior, minimal implementation makes it pass, and refactoring occurs only while tests remain green.

nodes.label: Test Pyramid
nodes.rationale: Most coverage belongs in fast unit tests, with progressively fewer integration and end-to-end tests for broader behavior.

nodes.label: Planning and Task Breakdown Skill Guide
nodes.norm_label: planning and task breakdown skill guide

nodes.label: Fresh-Context Adversarial Review
nodes.rationale: A fresh reviewer biased to disprove catches assumptions and hidden coupling that accumulated session context may silently turn into facts.

nodes.label: Atomic Commits
nodes.rationale: Each commit should represent one logical change so it remains reviewable, revertible, and understandable in history.

nodes.label: Trunk-Based Development
nodes.rationale: Keeping main deployable and integrating through short-lived branches limits divergence, merge conflict, and integration delay.

nodes.label: Feature Flag Rollout
nodes.rationale: Deploy inactive code, enable it for internal users, progress through canary percentages, monitor each stage, and remove the flag after full rollout.

nodes.label: Pro Beta Channel Gating
nodes.rationale: Stable is the default channel, while beta requires a Pro license key or the custom User-Agent and returns pro_required when unauthorized.

nodes.label: Signed Background Update
nodes.rationale: After one native permission choice, the updater downloads in the background, verifies a minisign signature against the embedded public key, installs, and restarts automatically.

nodes.label: Dual-Surface Delivery
nodes.rationale: The same terminal experience is delivered through a browser-served Vite app at /code and an Electron arm64 DMG at /releases.

nodes.label: Git Workflow and Versioning Skill Guide
nodes.norm_label: git workflow and versioning skill guide

nodes.label: Short-Lived Feature Branches
nodes.rationale: Feature branches should merge within one to three days; feature flags are preferred over keeping incomplete work on a branch for weeks.

nodes.label: Reversible Incremental Launch
nodes.rationale: A production launch should be observable, incremental, and reversible rather than a one-time deployment.

nodes.label: Server-Medicated Update Feed
nodes.rationale: The desktop polls the Vibecoder site rather than GitHub so routing, channel gating, and emergency corrections can change without shipping a new app binary.

nodes.label: Component Composition
nodes.rationale: Focused composable components, separated data and presentation layers, and the simplest adequate state model keep interfaces maintainable and avoid configuration-heavy abstractions.

nodes.label: PTY-Backed Opencode
nodes.rationale: Both surfaces wrap the real opencode CLI through node-pty rather than reimplementing the agent, with missing-binary and PATH override handling.

nodes.label: Transport Abstraction
nodes.rationale: A single Transport contract decouples the React terminal UI from WebSocket and Electron IPC implementations while preserving identical connect, write, resize, and event behavior.

nodes.label: Particle Globe
nodes.rationale: A deterministic Fibonacci-sphere point cloud rotates in three dimensions, depth-buckets rendering, and animates network arcs and pulses.

nodes.label: Ten-Second Canvas Storyboard
nodes.rationale: A fixed ten-second timeline moves from branded globe formation to headline, terminal work, product benefits, call to action, and closing frame.

nodes.label: Terminal Agent Demonstration
nodes.rationale: Typed commands and timed output show the local coding agent reading files, planning changes, and editing a Stripe checkout example.

nodes.label: Replica Security and Failure Constraints
nodes.rationale: The PTY binds only to loopback, Electron isolates context and disables Node integration, and reconnect, resize, exit, concurrency, and missing-agent paths are explicit review concerns.

nodes.label: Deterministic Animation Timeline
nodes.rationale: Seeded randomness and time-parameterized interpolation keep the promotional render reproducible while easing functions control visual pacing.

nodes.label: Structural Review Remedies
nodes.rationale: A review finding should name a structural move that removes branches, concepts, duplication, or misplaced feature logic.

nodes.label: Verification Evidence in Review
nodes.rationale: A review verdict must inspect the tests, build, manual checks, screenshots, dependency changes, and stated verification evidence.

nodes.label: Incremental Simplification Process
nodes.rationale: Understand first, identify concrete complexity signals, apply one change at a time, and verify after each step.

nodes.label: Scoped Simplification and Dead Code Hygiene
nodes.norm_label: scoped simplification and dead code hygiene
nodes.rationale: Limit refactoring to changed work, remove confirmed dead code, and avoid unrelated churn that obscures the review.

nodes.label: Selective Context Packing
nodes.rationale: Use task-shaped context blocks and summaries rather than flooding the agent with unrelated files or stale conversation.

nodes.label: Root-Cause Fix and Regression Guard
nodes.rationale: Fix the underlying cause, add a regression test that fails without the fix, and verify the original scenario and the full suite.

nodes.label: Stop-the-Line Debugging Workflow
nodes.rationale: Unexpected errors stop feature work so evidence is preserved, diagnosed, fixed at the root, guarded against recurrence, and verified end to end.

nodes.label: Systematic Error Triage
nodes.rationale: Reproduce, localize, and reduce failures before proposing a fix, using minimal cases to distinguish causes from symptoms.

nodes.label: Design System Adherence
nodes.rationale: Production UI should follow the product's actual tokens, content, accessibility requirements, and interaction patterns rather than generic AI aesthetics.

nodes.label: Billing Plan Comparison
nodes.rationale: Responsive plan cards, a monthly-yearly billing switch, a featured tier, and a cost table make pricing differences easy to scan.

nodes.label: Credit Meter States
nodes.rationale: Green, warning, and depleted colors distinguish healthy, low, and exhausted balances while captions and out-of-credit actions preserve meaning beyond color.

nodes.label: Credits Cost Simulator
nodes.rationale: Interactive credit actions, a running balance, consumption meter, refill indicator, and event log demonstrate how usage and depletion affect the user.

nodes.label: Reference-Led Design Contract
nodes.rationale: Studying a few relevant references before implementation turns hierarchy, density, controls, states, and responsive rules into an explicit design contract without copying proprietary branding or layouts.

nodes.label: Responsive Accessible Pricing UI
nodes.rationale: Fluid type and grids, visible focus states, ARIA switch state, reduced-transparency handling, and mobile navigation prioritize access and responsive use.

nodes.label: Idea Refine One-Pager Artifact
nodes.rationale: The final artifact captures a problem statement, recommended direction, assumptions, MVP scope, and an explicit not-doing list, and is saved only after confirmation.

nodes.label: MVP Scoping Principles
nodes.rationale: An MVP should do one user job well, test the riskiest assumption, be time-boxed, and carry a mandatory not-doing list.

nodes.label: Interactive User Requirement Discovery
nodes.rationale: The skill asks a small set of targeted questions about audience, success, constraints, prior attempts, and timing before proposing a direction.

nodes.label: Idea Refine Three-Phase Workflow
nodes.rationale: Raw ideas are expanded, evaluated, and sharpened through structured divergent and convergent thinking rather than jumping directly to implementation.

nodes.label: Ninety-Five Percent Confidence Gate
nodes.rationale: Interviewing is complete only when the agent can predict the user's response to the next three relevant questions, rather than merely feeling more certain.

nodes.label: One-Question Interview
nodes.rationale: Asking one focused question at a time with an explicit guess exposes assumptions while preserving the user's ability to react and redirect the framing.

nodes.label: Confirmed Statement of Intent
nodes.rationale: The interview ends with the user's outcome, audience, motivation, success criteria, binding constraint, and explicit out-of-scope boundary, confirmed with an unambiguous yes.

nodes.label: Capability Map
nodes.rationale: Multi-capability initiatives are decomposed into stable modules with explicit responsibilities, one-way dependencies, and a gated build order.

nodes.label: Gated Specify Plan Tasks Implement
nodes.rationale: Each phase produces an explicit artifact and waits for human validation before downstream specification, planning, task creation, or implementation begins.

nodes.label: Human Review Gates
nodes.rationale: Assumptions and expensive boundaries are surfaced before coding, while validation at every phase prevents a mistaken premise from propagating through the project.

nodes.label: Dark-Background Display Context
nodes.rationale: The only visible mark is filled white and no opaque background rectangle is present, making the asset most legible on a dark or contrasting backdrop; its actual rendering context is not included.

nodes.label: Vercel Triangle Logomark
nodes.rationale: The filename explicitly names Vercel, and the single upward-pointing triangular path matches the Vercel logomark, supporting identification as brand artwork rather than a generic geometric illustration.

nodes.label: Public Static Web Asset
nodes.rationale: Its location in the repository's public directory indicates a browser-servable static asset intended for web presentation, though no consuming component is shown in this file.

nodes.label: Generic File Interface Indicator
nodes.rationale: The page silhouette, folded corner, and text-line marks form a conventional document glyph, while the compact 16×16 single-gray presentation makes the asset most suitable as a neutral file-related interface indicator rather than a specific file type or richly illustrated graphic.

nodes.label: Compact Interface Icon
nodes.rationale: The 16 by 16 viewBox, simple monochrome paths, and public asset location indicate a compact reusable web interface graphic, although no consuming component is available to confirm its role.

nodes.label: Globe Grid Design
nodes.rationale: A solid gray circular silhouette is segmented by negative-space curved longitude lines and horizontal latitude bands to make the globe recognizable at small sizes.

nodes.label: Worldwide Representation
nodes.rationale: The circular globe silhouette explicitly represents global scope and commonly signals international, language, region, or network concepts; the exact interface use is not shown by the isolated asset.

nodes.label: Next.js Brand Identification
nodes.rationale: The asset serves as a compact brand mark for visually identifying Next.js, rather than depicting a product UI, data, or explanatory diagram.

nodes.label: Black Monochrome Brand Styling
nodes.rationale: The entire mark uses a single solid black fill (#000) on a transparent background, with no gradients, shadows, outlines, or additional colors.

nodes.label: NEXT.js Wordmark
nodes.rationale: The central visual element is the name NEXT in wide geometric uppercase forms followed by a lowercase dotted j and rounded lowercase s.

nodes.label: NEXT.js SVG Logo Asset
nodes.rationale: A 394×80 web-ready SVG stored in the public asset directory. Its solid black NEXT.js wordmark and transparent canvas indicate that it is intended to display Next.js brand identity in a web interface.

nodes.label: Untrusted Browser Content Boundary
nodes.rationale: DOM, console, network, and JavaScript results are untrusted data; browser instructions, secrets, external navigation, and mutations require explicit boundaries.

nodes.label: Untrusted External Context
nodes.rationale: Configuration, data, external documentation, and tool results may contain instruction-like text and must be treated as data with explicit trust boundaries.

nodes.label: Untrusted Error Output
nodes.rationale: Logs, stack traces, and external errors are diagnostic data, not instructions, and embedded commands or URLs require verification and user confirmation.

nodes.label: Five Cheap-Road-to-Green Moves
nodes.rationale: The floor guard detects suppressed checkers, unfinished work, skipped or weakened tests, lowered constraints, and new exceptions with explicit exit codes.

nodes.label: Guard the Quality Bar
nodes.rationale: Review should loudly catch lowered thresholds, easier tests, silenced checkers, unfinished work, and untracked exceptions while silent changes tighten the bar.

nodes.label: Context Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Persistent rules, relevant specs, source files, focused errors, and only necessary conversation history are deliberately ordered by task relevance.

nodes.label: Next.js Breaking-Changes Rules
nodes.rationale: Agents must read the local Next.js documentation before writing code because this version has breaking APIs, conventions, and file structure; the generated block is retained to prevent it from being recreated as an uncommitted change.

nodes.label: Window Frame
nodes.rationale: The nested rectangular silhouette defines the window boundary and suggests an inset content area.

nodes.label: Three Header Control Dots
nodes.rationale: Three evenly spaced dots in the upper-left create a familiar window or browser header motif.

nodes.label: Window Icon
nodes.rationale: A compact 16 by 16 monochrome SVG whose framed shape and header dots make it a user-interface symbol for a browser or application window.

nodes.label: Boundary Validation
nodes.rationale: Validate user input, external responses, and environment configuration at system edges before trusted internal logic consumes them.

nodes.label: Contract-First Interface Design
nodes.rationale: Public interfaces should be defined as contracts before implementation, with additive changes and consistent input and output types.

nodes.label: Idempotency and Unknown Outcomes
nodes.rationale: Retries need a stable idempotency key, atomic claim, payload guard, deliberate duplicate handling, and explicit treatment of a third outcome: unknown.

nodes.label: Clean Runtime Acceptance Bar
nodes.rationale: A production page should have a clean console, expected network responses, visual evidence, accessible structure, and measured performance.

nodes.label: Browser Runtime Verification Workflow
nodes.rationale: Reproduce, inspect, diagnose, fix, and verify browser behavior using live DOM, console, network, performance, and accessibility evidence.

nodes.label: Staged Deployment and Rollback
nodes.rationale: Preview, staging, canary, and production stages make releases reversible; rollback is a first-class deployment capability.

nodes.label: Environment and Secret Management
nodes.rationale: Local, test, CI, and production environments use separate secret stores, and production credentials never belong in CI or source.

nodes.label: Automated Quality Gate Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Lint, types, tests, build, integration, security, and size checks shift quality enforcement left and block weak changes.

nodes.label: Five-Axis Code Review
nodes.rationale: Review combines correctness, readability, architecture, security, and performance rather than treating passing tests as sufficient approval.

nodes.label: Behavior-Preserving Simplification
nodes.rationale: Simplification must preserve outputs, errors, side effects, ordering, and edge cases while improving comprehension speed and matching project conventions.

nodes.label: Quality Ratchets and Check Cost Placement
nodes.norm_label: quality ratchets and check cost placement
nodes.rationale: Fast checks belong near edits, expensive checks belong later, and measured ratchets prevent unstated quality regression.

nodes.label: Written Quality Contract
nodes.rationale: A written, command-backed quality contract makes the project bar durable across agents and separates enforceable numbers from aspirations.

nodes.label: Durable Session Handoff
nodes.rationale: At a task boundary, persist scope, status, changed files, verification, risks, and approvals so a fresh session can resume from durable state.

nodes.label: Agent Replica Failure Recovery
nodes.rationale: Missing binaries, PTY exits, WebSocket disconnects, and unavailable servers each receive an explicit recoverable UI state.

nodes.label: Agent Replica Security Boundary
nodes.rationale: The PTY uses the user's existing trust model, the WebSocket binds to localhost, and Electron exposes only a narrow preload bridge with context isolation.

nodes.label: Shared PTY Transport Abstraction
nodes.rationale: The browser and Electron targets share the same React components and transport interface while swapping WebSocket and IPC implementations.

nodes.label: Path Sandbox Validation
nodes.rationale: Dynamic file paths are revalidated against a sandbox rule before storage, and invalid paths store nothing.

nodes.label: Session Ownership Model
nodes.rationale: Requests under the app are gated by an unexpired session cookie, and every read and write is scoped to the session user on the server.

nodes.label: Transactional Prompt Change Flow
nodes.rationale: Prompt generation writes validated, unapplied changes transactionally; explicit apply and revert routes preserve the last good project state.

nodes.label: Multiplatform Build and Publish
nodes.rationale: A matrix builds signed macOS, Windows, and Linux bundles, canonicalizes updater assets, and publishes stable or prerelease GitHub releases with latest.json.

nodes.label: Release Preflight and Signing Gate
nodes.rationale: A release must match the app version, enable compatible updater artifacts, and possess the Tauri updater signing key before build jobs start.

nodes.label: Accessible Landing Implementation Notes
nodes.rationale: Heading order, list semantics, accessible names, contrast, dynamic numbers, and reduced motion are explicit implementation requirements.

nodes.label: Credit Config as Single Source of Truth
nodes.norm_label: credit config as single source of truth
nodes.rationale: Dynamic grant and price values must come from the credit configuration used by billing, so the landing page and billing engine cannot disagree.

nodes.label: Inclusive Free Tier
nodes.rationale: The free tier is presented as a genuinely usable product rather than a demo, with daily credits as the only meter and no card or ads.

nodes.label: No-Dark-Patterns Checklist
nodes.rationale: Implementation explicitly rejects scarcity pressure, hidden opt-ins, confirm-shaming, and buried credit expiry, and requires cancel parity with signup.

nodes.label: Plain, Warm, Exact Voice
nodes.rationale: Short, warm, plain-language copy with a grade 7-8 reading level signals honesty and avoids pressure or celebratory trapping.

nodes.label: Reviewable and Reversible Trust Features
nodes.rationale: Review-before-apply changes, byte-for-byte restoration, accessible output, and code export form the product trust promise.

nodes.label: Trust and Ownership Differentiation
nodes.rationale: Vibecoder differentiates through transparent economics, code ownership, accessibility, and a reviewable, reversible agent loop rather than ads or region locks.

nodes.label: Reviewable Generation Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Prompts plan changes, record validated file operations, pass a build gate, snapshot a version, and refresh preview so failed generation cannot leave a half-written project.

nodes.label: Vibecoder Acceptance Criteria
nodes.rationale: The quality bar combines clean lint and build, strict types, behavioral tests, tenant isolation, sandbox safety, accessibility, and crash recovery.

nodes.label: Model Provider Reliability Rules
nodes.rationale: Retries are limited to transient overload responses, respect Retry-After and time budgets, try other free providers without paid fallback, and distinguish accounting failure from provider billing behavior.
